name: Tube Investments of India Ltd
about: Tube Investments of India Limited (TII) is one of India’s leading manufacturers of a wide range of products for major industries such as Automotive, Railway, Construction, Mining, Agriculture, etc. The Company’s 3 main verticals are Engineering, Metal Formed Products and Bicycles. In line with its growth strategies, the Company has forayed into TMT bars and Truck Body Building business and is additionally exploring opportunities in optic lens and other vision systems for the Auto industry. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 30.3% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 31.3%.
EBITDA margin held roughly flat over 5 years (10.5% → 10.0%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 21% to 33% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Over 5 years: ₹6,211 cr of profit, ₹5,303 cr of operating cash — conversion 0.85x, adequate.

ledger.quote: at a consol level, to do double digit, higher double digit growth
ledger.statement: Consolidated double-digit (higher double-digit) growth in revenue, top line and bottom line
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32.7% and PAT 39.4% YoY (F:rev_yoy_last_q_pct, F:pat_yoy_last_q_pct). This has not held historically: 3-year PAT CAGR is -5.5% (F:pat_cagr_3y), and standalone PBT rose only 1.2% in Q2 (C1).

ledger.quote: we are targeting about 85% to PAT
ledger.statement: Internal cash conversion target of about 85% of PAT
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: 5-year CFO/PAT is 0.85 (F:cfo_to_pat_5y), exactly the target. Working capital has loosened, though, with CCC at 41 days against 17 three years ago (F:ccc_days_latest, F:ccc_days_3y_ago).

ledger.quote: our perspective in the medical business will be higher double digit teen numbers
ledger.statement: Medical business profitability at a higher double-digit teen level once stabilised
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: Management says it 'will take some time to stabilize' (C5). Medical margins are not disclosed in the inputs.

ledger.quote: we are confident we will be able to recover fully, in the next one or two quarters
ledger.statement: Full recovery of commodity cost increases through customer price settlements within one to two quarters
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: Made on the Q2 FY27 call, and the gap is visible: standalone revenue rose 27.9% but PBT only 1.2%, and Engineering PBIT margin fell to 9.4% from 11.9% (C1).

ledger.quote: We are hopeful by end of current quarter, which is Q3, the team will be in place
ledger.statement: Medical business sales team in place by end of Q3FY27
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: Due by end Q3 FY27 (December 2026), with no update since the Q2 FY27 call (C3).

ledger.quote: we are going to do the commercial production from our Naidupet facility starting next quarter
ledger.statement: CDMO commercial production from Naidupet facility to start in Q1FY27
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: The Q1 FY27 deadline has passed. At the Q2 FY27 call the semi-commercial plant had supplied a customer, but validation batches were still finishing and were due to move into the clean room 'in the next three to four weeks' (C4), so commercial production had not started. C4 doesn't name Naidupet; matching it to this promise is an inference.
ledger.actual_text: Validation batches still running at the Q2 FY27 call

ledger.quote: capex in our core business will be around Rs.300 Crores to Rs.350 Crores range
ledger.statement: Core business capex of INR 300-350 crore in FY27
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: No capex figure is in the inputs, and FY27 ends in March 2027. Standalone free cash flow was Rs167 crore in Q2 FY27 (C1).

ledger.quote: We are confident to grow the business between the range of 15% to 20%
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: The wound-care/sutures business is growing '20% plus', and grew 20% last quarter (C3), at the top of the 15-20% range.

ledger.quote: hopeful will give 20% year-on-year growth in TI Medical going forward
ledger.statement: TI Medical growth of 20% year on year
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: The 20% in C3 is for the wound-care/sutures company. Growth for TI Medical as a whole, including the newly acquired IV cannula unit, isn't given.

ledger.quote: we are going to finish even the plant approvals for whatever assets we have purchased which will be done during the quarter
ledger.statement: Plant approvals for IV cannula assets acquired to be completed in Q1FY27
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: Q1 FY27 has ended. The Q2 FY27 call talks about staffing the IV cannula business and lifting utilisation of the current facility (C3) but doesn't mention the plant approvals.

ledger.quote: as we end this particular quarter, Q1, we will be back to our normal production capacity on the supply side
ledger.statement: Supply issue resolved; normal production capacity restored by end of Q1FY27
ledger.speaker: Jalaj Gupta
ledger.evidence: At the Q4 FY26 call, output had reached targeted levels in April-May (C7). Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue growth accelerated to 32.7% from 17.1% in Q1 (F:rev_yoy_last4_pct), consistent with restored supply, but no later call excerpt confirms it.

ledger.quote: by end of this financial year or middle of next financial year, it will be 100% utilized
ledger.statement: CRSS plant in Nashik to reach 100% utilisation by Mar-2027 to mid-FY28
ledger.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
ledger.evidence: The window ends between March 2027 and mid-FY28, and no utilisation data is in the inputs.

ledger.quote: So at least the team should be on board in the first quarter of FY2027.
ledger.statement: Key people for the services business to be on board by Q1FY27
ledger.speaker: Vellayan Subbiah
ledger.evidence: Q1 FY27 has ended, and the inputs don't mention the services-business hires again.

ledger.quote: the two which we are pushing towards breakeven in the next 12 to 18 will be in the heavy vehicles and in the three-wheeler
ledger.statement: Heavy vehicles and three-wheeler businesses to reach breakeven within 12-18 months
ledger.speaker: Vellayan Subbiah
ledger.evidence: The 12-18 month window from the Q3 FY26 call is still open. EV business P&L is not in the inputs.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management is upbeat on double-digit growth, 85% cash conversion and medical margins, while declining to give top-line projections and saying the medical build-out will take time.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management is very confident that the supply issue is resolved and that volumes will scale up, and is bullish on TI Medical growth (p7-35-1, p8-39-2).

tones.label: mixed
tones.why: Management targets breakeven for two businesses within 12-18 months, though it concedes that one item is taking longer than expected.

context.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
context.text: Yes, good morning, everybody. I would like to share the Board of Directors of TI met yesterday and approved the financial results of the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Standalone results for the quarter, revenue for Q2 was at Rs.2710 Crores, against Rs.2119 Crores in the same period previous year. PBT was at Rs.253 Crores against Rs.250 Crores in the same period of previous year. ROIC stood at 44% for the quarter, ended September 30, 2026, which is the same as the previous year same quarter. Free cash flow for the quarter was Rs.167 Crores. I will give a view about the business wise. Engineering division, the revenue for the quarter was Rs.1,828 Crores, compared to Rs.1,382 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Profit before interest and Tax for the quarter was Rs.171 Crores against Rs.164 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Metal formed product revenue for the quarter was Rs.473 Crores, compared with Rs.408 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Profit before interest and Tax for the quarter was Rs.49 Crores against Rs.44 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Mobility revenue for the quarter was Rs.247 Crores, compared with Rs.194 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Profit before interest and Tax for the quarter was Rs.8 Crores against Rs.4 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Others, revenue for the quarter was Rs.260 Crores, compared with Rs.227 Crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Profit before interest and tax for the quarter was Rs.20 Crores against Rs.18 Crores, in the same period for the previous year. context.speaker: Gopalakrishnan S
context.text: So, yes, first of all, thank you for the opportunity, and I wish the team all the best. My first question is I have seen that the operating margin is almost stagnant at 9% to 10%. Are there any plans in, Tube Investments to restructure the business. Like, for example, what, Mahindra did after Anish Shah took over like exiting some businesses like Ssangyong and Mehru, and, making some acquisitions and businesses which cannot, achieve ROE of 18% were removed and all that. So, like that, whether any such restructuring plan is there for Tube Investments? That is, one point and second point is about, moat building. You know, I mean, whether, you are planning to build moat for the company, so that the growth can be more sustainable and profitable. That is all.

context.speaker: Mukesh Ahuja
context.text: I will go for second question, and then Mr. Jalaj can address the first question. Regarding TI Medical, as you are aware, maybe let us say around three years back, I guess, we acquired Lotus, which was basically wound care, invested into sutures business. I am happy to share that maybe that company is growing 20% plus now, and when you see in the last quarter also, the growth was 20% and also to grow this business further, we have invested into a plastic medical devices business including IV cannula and canister, where maybe, let us say, this was a very, very small startup, which we acquired it and we are building the company in terms of manpower and the sales team etc., and those efforts are on. We are hopeful by end of current quarter, which is Q3, the team will be in place. Then it is a question of, first bringing the capacity utilization for the current facility, what we enjoyed, and based on the progress, we will be further investing in that facility because the opportunity is very large for that company. So, we remain bullish about our medical business.

Sure, Mukesh, thank you. The semi-commercial plant has been already commissioned, and we have even supplied quantities to customer. In fact, one of the products which we had supplied from the semi-commercial plant, the customer has already given projection for the next calendar year, which is a financial year for the European customer. So, the clean room has also been commissioned, and right now, the validation batches in the intermediate block is nearing completion, then it will move into the clean room in the next three to four weeks.

So, like, it will take some time to stabilize, but maybe let us say our perspective in the medical business will be higher double digit teen numbers, that will be the profitability level for the business.

So, as of now, we are able to maintain around 15% of our revenues are coming from exports at a TI level and, in spite of various, issues in the geopolitical issues, we are able to maintain that number. Obviously, like you rightly said that our initial endeavor was to grow this towards 20%, but which did not happen. While the growth is happening, export pie is maintained. We are looking for, maybe, let us say, that if some stabilization in the geopolitical situation happens, we see customer engagements and contracts are running in good. We have not seen, maybe, irrespective of the situation, the customers walking it out.

It is very close to our existing unit where we make our three wheeler and now we are running the facility and is the reason and whatever we have seen in the month of April and up till now in the month of May, we have been able to ramp up to the levels that we had targeted for. There are still some more teething issues to be resolved. So that is the reason we are very confident by end of this quarter, we will be able to resolve by and large this specific issue of body invite.

So Hyundai has just started maybe last quarter only their Western plant and we are already servicing requirements from our facility in Pune. Obviously, it will go through a ramp up phase, but all those issues we feel in Q1 ramp up issues and some teething issues, whenever you start a plant, will be getting settled in current quarter.

Okay, so I will take the second question first, so today we cater to about, so we have about 117 dealerships in E3-wheeler and we cater to in the L5M category about 65% to 70% of the TIV is what this particular 117 dealers they cater to. Within these dealerships also, we are trying to have a focused dealer approach to ramp up our volumes, which is to say about 52% to 55% of these dealers is what we are primarily focusing more on, which can give us about, let’s say, 75% of the volumes that we do.

business.what_it_does: Diversified manufacturer whose standalone segments are Engineering, Metal Formed Products, Mobility and Others. The group is also building a medical business (sutures/wound care, IV cannula), a CDMO plant, electric three-wheeler and heavy-vehicle businesses, and a CRSS plant in Nashik.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.comment: Shares are of the Rs2,808 crore standalone Q2 FY27 segment total before eliminations; standalone revenue was Rs2,710 crore. Revenue Rs1,828 crore (+32% YoY); PBIT Rs171 crore (+4%), so PBIT margin fell to 9.4% from 11.9% (C1).

segments.name: Metal Formed Products
segments.comment: Revenue Rs473 crore (+16% YoY); PBIT Rs49 crore against Rs44 crore (C1).

segments.name: Mobility
segments.comment: Revenue Rs247 crore (+27% YoY); PBIT Rs8 crore against Rs4 crore (C1).

segments.name: Others
segments.comment: Revenue Rs260 crore against Rs227 crore (C1).

segments.name: TI Medical
segments.comment: Consolidated, share not stated. Sutures/wound care growing ~20%, and the IV cannula unit is being staffed (C3). Targeted at high-teens profitability (C5).

segments.name: CDMO
segments.comment: Consolidated, share not stated. The semi-commercial plant is commissioned and supplying; validation batches are under way (C4).

segments.name: EV three-wheeler and heavy vehicles
segments.comment: Consolidated, share not stated. 117 three-wheeler dealerships (C9). Breakeven targeted within 12-18 months of the Q3 FY26 call (G14).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Higher double-digit consolidated growth in both top line and bottom line (G1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32.7% and PAT 39.4%. Over three years, though, PAT CAGR is -5.5% against revenue CAGR of 15.1%, so the recent quarter breaks a longer trend.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Commodity cost increases will be fully recovered through customer price settlements within one to two quarters (G4).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Standalone Q2 revenue rose 27.9% but PBT only 1.2%, and Engineering PBIT margin was 9.4% against 11.9%. The consolidated margin has sat between 8.8% and 10.1% for four quarters and is 260bps below three years ago.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: The export share is being held at ~15% despite geopolitical issues (C6).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Management itself says the original aim of taking exports to 20% of revenue 'did not happen' (C6). The facts contain no export revenue figure to test it further.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Cash conversion of about 85% of PAT (G2).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: 5-year CFO/PAT is 0.85, 5-year FCF Rs1,141 crore, and Q2 standalone FCF Rs167 crore. CCC has stretched to 41 days from 17 three years ago.

bull.point: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32.7% and PAT 39.4%, and standalone Engineering revenue grew 32% to Rs1,828 crore.
Leverage is low and cash conversion on target: D/E is 0.11 on Rs910 crore of borrowings, 5-year CFO/PAT is 0.85 against an 85% goal, and Q2 brought Rs167 crore of standalone FCF at a 44% ROIC.

Medical and CDMO optionality: sutures are growing ~20% (top of the 15-20% guide), the CDMO semi-commercial plant has shipped to a European customer that has given next-year projections, and medical is targeted at high-teens profitability.

bear.point: Margins are stuck: the consolidated margin has been 8.8-10.1% over the last four quarters and is 260bps lower than three years ago, and 3-year PAT CAGR is -5.5%.

Growth is not reaching standalone profit: Q2 revenue rose 27.9% but PBT only 1.2%, and Engineering PBIT margin fell to 9.4% from 11.9%. Recovery depends on customer price settlements within one to two quarters.
Dated milestones slip: CDMO commercial production promised for Q1 FY27 was still in validation at the Q2 call, the 20% export-share aim is stuck at ~15%, and CCC has risen to 41 days from 17.

questions: How much of the Engineering PBIT margin drop from 11.9% to 9.4% is unrecovered commodity cost, how much is already settled with customers, and what margin should Q4 FY27 show once it is recovered?
Having missed Q1 FY27, when does the CDMO plant start commercial production, and how much revenue is contracted with the European customer for next year?
What are the current losses in the electric three-wheeler and heavy-vehicle businesses, and what monthly volume gets each to the breakeven promised within 12-18 months of the Q3 FY26 call?
